Whether the defendant has any right to continue the occupation in the suit property i.e. Flat no. 73-C, II Floor, MIG Flats,
Block-3, Lawrence Road, Delhi on the basis of the oral mutual settlement ? (OPD).
24.
The issue no
. 2 is taken up first.
The onus of proving the issue is on the defendants.
The defendants have admitted execution of relinquishment deed in favour of the plaintiff.

The defence of the defendants is that the relinquishment deed is contrary to the oral mutual family settlement as per which it was agreed that the defendants will be given their share after the sale of the suit property.
It is their case that the relinquishment deed was never meant to be without consideration.
25. The counter claim of the defendants for seeking cancellation of the relinquishment deed has been dismissed by this court.

The defendants to prove the oral family settlement have examined witnesses who deposed on affidavit before the court that there was an oral mutual understanding between the plaintiff, defendants and other co-owners that the sale proceeds of the suit property will be distributed proportionately to their respective shares and the defendants shall continue to live in the suit property until the same is jointly sold and the sale proceeds are divided between all the co-owners.
All the witnesses DW-1 to DW-4 have made the same submission in their affidavits.
Further, all the defendant witnesses have also admitted to the execution of the relinquishment deed and also their signatures on the same.
26. In the relinquishment deed Ex. PW-1/1 it is only stated that defendant no. 1 wants to relinquish her share and no consideration against the same is mentioned.

Similarly, other NAINA GUPTA Date:
GUPTA 2025.03.05 16:44:43 +0530 parties to the relinquishment deed including witnesses DW-2 Sh. Mohan Singh, DW-3 Ms. Sukhvinder Kaur also relinquished their share in the suit property.

27. When the execution of the relinquishment deed is undisputed and the counter claim of the defendants to cancel the same has been dismissed, can the defendants rely upon the alleged oral mutual settlement between the parties ?

Under section 91 of the Indian Evidence Act when the terms of the contract have been reduced to a form of document, no evidence can be given in proof of the terms of the said contract except the document itself or secondary evidence of its contents in cases in which secondary evidence is permissible.

Under section of 92 of the Indian Evidence Act,
there is further bar on admission of any evidence of any oral agreement for the purposes of contradicting varying, adding to or subtracting from the terms of any written contract, grant or other dispossession of property.
28. In the present case the relinquishment deed was executed and registered between the parties without any consideration.
Therefore, any oral evidence to the effect that the relinquishment deed was signed subject to consideration is barred under section 92 as it contradicts the terms of the relinquishment deed.

Therefore, the oral evidence led on behalf of the defendants to prove the Jhujhar Singh vs Sarabjit Kaur And Ors on 5 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10967700/

Whether the plaintiff is entitled for decree of mandatory injunction as prayed for ? (OPP)
30.
The burden to prove this issue is upon the plaintiff.
The defendants have failed to prove their case that they have right to reside in the suit property on the basis of the oral mutual settlement between the parties.
However, the plaintiff must stand on his own legs and prove his case on the scale of preponderance of probabilities.

31. The plaintiff has filed the present case for seeking mandatory injunction on the basis that there exists a licensor licensee relationship between the parties since 2012 when the plaintiff permitted the defendants to reside in the suit property.
In contrary to the plaintiff's case the defendants have successfully proved that they have been in possession of the property much prior to 2012.
It is their case that they are in possession of the suit property since 2006.

To prove their possession in the suit property the defendants have led evidence evidencing that the son of the defendants is enrolled in school in Guru Harkishan Public School on the basis of the address of the suit property.

Further, the defendant no.1 and 2 examined as DW-1 and DW-3 NAINA by NAINA GUPTA GUPTA Date:
2025.03.05 16:44:54 +0530 respectively have produced on record original telephone bills Ex. DW-1/3 (Colly) showing that the bills in the suit property are in the name of defendant no. 2 ever since 2008.
Further the defendants have also produced the Residents Welfare Associations receipts showing that the monthly subscription is being deposited by defendant no. 2 since 09.12.2006.
At the time of exhibition of the documents no objection as to mode of proof of these documents was taken on behalf of Ld. Counsel for the plaintiff.

During arguments, it has been contended on behalf of plaintiff that since no witness has been examined from the Airtel company and the Residents Welfare Association the bills and receipts have not been proved as per law.

The documents sought to be placed on record are very much relevant to the present case and no objection regarding mode of proof was taken on behalf of the plaintiff during the exhibition of the documents.
If any objection was taken on behalf of the plaintiff, the defendants would have an opportunity to summon further witnesses.
Therefore, it is held that the defendants have successfully proved that they are in possession of the suit property prior to 2012.

sentences.text: Now the court must examine what was the nature of the possession of the defendants in the suit property.

As per the defendants own case the defendant no. 1 came to the suit property while Smt.
Satjit Kaur was alive and she started living in the suit property to take care of her in 2006.
Thus the initial possession of the defendants in the suit property was as a licensee of Smt. Satjit Kaur.

It is stated in the written statement that after the death of Smt. Satjit Kaur, the defendant no. 1 continued to stay in the suit property with the consent of all the co-owners as Digitally signed by NAINA NAINA Date:
GUPTA GUPTA
2025.03.05 16:45:01 +0530 the suit property was vacant and no one was available to take care of the same.
Thus, the possession of the defendants over the suit property continued to be permissive in nature.
The defendant no. 1 in her cross examination dated 15.07.2019 also stated that she had come to stay in the flat with the consent of the plaintiff.
The relevant paragraph from the cross examination is reproduced for ready reference:- "It is correct that the rental value of a flat in block B-3, Lawrence road is around 20000-25000 per month.
(vol. I have no rent agreement with plaintiff.
Again said I had come to stay in the flat with the consent of the plaintiff)."
33. When the possession of the defendant over the suit property was always permissive in nature she remained in the suit property nothing more than as a licensee.
It is not the case of the plaintiff or the defendants that the defendants are tresspassers in the suit property.

It is also not the case of the defendants that the plaintiff was required to file a suit for possession on the basis of title and for this reason alone a suit for mandatory injunction was not maintainable.
34.
The defendants' only case was that she was also a co- owner in the suit property which she failed to prove in light of the relinquishment deed executed by her in favour of the plaintiff.
Further, in 2006, Smt. Apjit Kaur, the mother of the defendant no.1 was alive and the defendant no. 1 did not become a co - owner in the suit property on account of death of Smt. Satjit Kaur.
Smt. Apjit Kaur expired on 17.03.2010.
Prioer to that the defendants had no right, title or interest in the suit property and were in possession only as licensees.

After the execution of the relinquishment deed,
no dispute with respect to title of the NAINA by NAINA GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.03.05 16:45:06 +0530 plaintiff in the suit property remains.
The defendant no. 1 at best only had 1/16th share in the suit property and as per her own case she remained in possession of the suit property with the consent of other co-owners.
Further, her defence is only that on sale of the suit property she was entitled to a share in the sale proceeds.
It has been held in the foregoing paragraphs that such a defence contrary to the registered relinquishment deed is legally impermissible.

35. In the land mark judgment of Sant Lal Jain vs Avtar Singh, 1985 AIR 857, it has been held that the principle of once a licensee always a licensee would apply to all kinds of licenses and after termination of the license, the licensee is under obligation to surrender its possession to the owner.

sentences.text: Further, it was also observed in this case that an attempt should be made to avoid multiplicity of the suits and a licensor should not be driven to file another round of suit.
The suit is in effect one for possession though couched in the form of suit for mandatory injunction.

sentences.text: In the facts of the present case, when there is no dispute of title remaining between the parties and the admitted position of the defendants is also that they are in the suit property with the consent of the other co-owners, I find that the plaintiff has successfully proved that there exists a licensor licensee relationship between them.

Further after the execution of the relinquishment deed in favour of the plaintiff on behalf of defendant no. 1 and other legal heirs, the plaintiff has stepped into the shoes of the original owner Smt. Satjit Kaur who had permitted the defendant no. 1 to reside in the suit property.
NAINA byGUPTA NAINA GUPTA 16:45:11 +0530 Date: 2025.03.05 37.
During arguments Ld. Counsel for the defendants has set up a case contrary to the one taken in the written statement filed on behalf of the defendants which is not permissible in law.
No arguments can be advanced beyond the pleadings.

In paragraph no. 3 of the plaint the plaintiff had stated that the suit property was transferred/inherited by Smt. Satjit Kaur after the death of Late Sh.
Tarlochan Singh.
This paragraph was admitted by the defendant in her written statement in paragraph no. 3.
Therefore the argument that on the death of Sh. Tarlochan Singh all his legal heirs became co-owners in the suit property is beyond the pleadings.

38. When the counter claim of the defendants for seeking cancellation of the relinquishment deed has been dismissed on account of being barred by limitation, the defendants cannot press that the relinquishment deed was obtained by fraud.
There was no requirement on behalf of the plaintiff to summon any attesting witnesses as the execution of the relinquishment deed was admitted by the defendants in their written statement.
Further, during defendants' evidence all the witnesses examined on behalf of the defendants admitted their signatures on the relinquishment deed and also admitted to executing the same.
39. The license of the defendants in the suit property was terminated on receipt of legal notice sent by the plaintiff on 11.07.2016.
In view of the termination of the license of the defendants the plaintiff is entitled to decree for mandatory injunction in his favour.
Accordingly, issue no. 1 is decided in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendants.

sentences.text: Further, the Court can take judicial notice that there had been steep rise in the rent of the properties in Delhi.

The Hon'ble Delhi High Court in Vinod Khanna v.
Bakshi Sachdev (Deceased) through LRs, AIR 1996 Delhi 32, has held that:
"21.
[I]t is true that no substantial evidence has been led by the plaintiffs in respect of the increase of rent in the properties like that of the suit property.

However, it is a well known fact that the amount of rent for various properties in and around Delhi has been rising staggeringly and we cannot see why such judicial notice could not be taken of the fact about such increase of rents in the premises in and around Delhi which is a city of growing importance being the capital of the country which is a matter of public history.
At this stage we may appropriately refer to the Court taking judicial notice of the increase of price of land rapidly in the urban areas in connection with the land acquisition matters.

Even the Apex Court NAINA by NAINA GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.03.05 16:45:21 +0530 has taken judicial notice of the fact of universal escalation of rent and even raised rent of disputed premises by taking such judicial notice in case of D.C. Oswal v. V.K. Subbiah, AIR 1992 SC 184 : 1992(1) RCR 326(SC).

entities.text: D.C. Oswal v. V.K. Subbiah, AIR 1992 SC 184 : 1992(1) RCR 326(SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
22. In that view of the matter we have no hesitation in our mind in holding that the trial court did not commit any illegality in taking judicial notice of the fact of increase of rents and determining the compensation in respect of the suit premises at Rs.10,000/- per month w.e.f. 19.1.1989, in view of the fact that the rent fixed for the said premises was at Rs. 6,000/- per month as far back as in the year 1974".
42.

Hence considering the above said legal position and the admission of defendant no. 1 in the present case, the Court is of the view that the plaintiff is entitled to mesne profits at rate of Rs.25,000 per month from 01.08.2016 till the handing over of the suit property by the defendants to plaintiff.

43. In view of the above discussion, this court is of the opinion that the plaintiff has discharged the burden of proof placed upon him and the suit of the plaintiff is decreed as follows:-
i.

The plaintiff is entitled to decree of mandatory injunction directing the defendants to vacate the suit property flat No.73-C, 2nd floor, MIG flats at block B-3, Lawrance Road, New Delhi and remove all their belongings.
ii. The plaintiff is entitled to mesne profits at rate of Rs.25,000/- per month from 01.08.2016 till the handing over of the suit property by the defendant to plaintiff.
The decree be executed only after payment of appropriate court fee.
44. The plaintiff shall also be entitled to costs of the suit.
Decree sheet be prepared accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The counter claim filed by the defendants was dismissed vide order dated 04.07.2017 on the ground that the same was time barred being filed after three years from the date of execution of relinquishment deed dated 08.06.2012.
The defendants have admitted execution of relinquishment deed in favour of the plaintiff.
In view of the findings on issue no. 1 and 2 the plaintiff is entitled to decree in his favour directing the defendants to vacate the suit property.
The plaintiff is also further entitled to mesne profits towards use and occupation of the suit property from 01.08.2016 till the vacation of the suit property by the defendants.
opennyai_summary.issue:
15. The court framed issues vide order dated 28.08.2017 as follows:-
i. Whether the plaintiff is entitled for decree of mandatory injunction as prayed for ?
Whether the defendant has any right to continue the occupation in the suit property i.e. Flat no. 73-C, II Floor, MIG Flats, Block-3, Lawrence Road, Delhi on the basis of the oral mutual settlement ?
Whether the defendant has any right to continue the occupation in the suit property i.e. Flat no. 73-C, II Floor, MIG Flats,
Block-3, Lawrence Road, Delhi on the basis of the oral mutual settlement ? (OPD).
24.
27. When the execution of the relinquishment deed is undisputed and the counter claim of the defendants to cancel the same has been dismissed, can the defendants rely upon the alleged oral mutual settlement between the parties ?
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The plaintiff has failed to prove that he gave the possession of the suit property to the defendants on license in 2012.
The defence of the defendants is that the relinquishment deed is contrary to the oral mutual family settlement as per which it was agreed that the defendants will be given their share after the sale of the suit property.
However, the plaintiff must stand on his own legs and prove his case on the scale of preponderance of probabilities.
31. The plaintiff has filed the present case for seeking mandatory injunction on the basis that there exists a licensor licensee relationship between the parties since 2012 when the plaintiff permitted the defendants to reside in the suit property.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The onus of proving the issue is on the defendants.
Under section 91 of the Indian Evidence Act when the terms of the contract have been reduced to a form of document, no evidence can be given in proof of the terms of the said contract except the document itself or secondary evidence of its contents in cases in which secondary evidence is permissible.
Therefore, any oral evidence to the effect that the relinquishment deed was signed subject to consideration is barred under section 92 as it contradicts the terms of the relinquishment deed.
Whether the plaintiff is entitled for decree of mandatory injunction as prayed for ? (OPP)
30.
The defendants have failed to prove their case that they have right to reside in the suit property on the basis of the oral mutual settlement between the parties.
Therefore, it is held that the defendants have successfully proved that they are in possession of the suit property prior to 2012.
As per the defendants own case the defendant no. 1 came to the suit property while Smt.
Satjit Kaur was alive and she started living in the suit property to take care of her in 2006.
Thus the initial possession of the defendants in the suit property was as a licensee of Smt. Satjit Kaur.
It is also not the case of the defendants that the plaintiff was required to file a suit for possession on the basis of title and for this reason alone a suit for mandatory injunction was not maintainable.
34.
The defendants' only case was that she was also a co- owner in the suit property which she failed to prove in light of the relinquishment deed executed by her in favour of the plaintiff.
Further, in 2006, Smt. Apjit Kaur, the mother of the defendant no.1 was alive and the defendant no. 1 did not become a co - owner in the suit property on account of death of Smt. Satjit Kaur.
The defendant no. 1 at best only had 1/16th share in the suit property and as per her own case she remained in possession of the suit property with the consent of other co-owners.
Further, her defence is only that on sale of the suit property she was entitled to a share in the sale proceeds.
35. In the land mark judgment of Sant Lal Jain vs Avtar Singh, 1985 AIR 857, it has been held that the principle of once a licensee always a licensee would apply to all kinds of licenses and after termination of the license, the licensee is under obligation to surrender its possession to the owner.
No separate evidence was led on behalf of the plaintiff to prove the actual rate of rent of the suit property or any other property in the vicinity of the suit property.
The Hon'ble Delhi High Court in Vinod Khanna v.

Hence considering the above said legal position and the admission of defendant no. 1 in the present case, the Court is of the view that the plaintiff is entitled to mesne profits at rate of Rs.25,000 per month from 01.08.2016 till the handing over of the suit property by the defendants to plaintiff.
opennyai_summary.decision:
In view of the termination of the license of the defendants the plaintiff is entitled to decree for mandatory injunction in his favour.
Accordingly, issue no. 1 is decided in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendants.
The plaintiff is entitled to decree of mandatory injunction directing the defendants to vacate the suit property flat No.73-C, 2nd floor, MIG flats at block B-3, Lawrance Road, New Delhi and remove all their belongings.
ii. The plaintiff is entitled to mesne profits at rate of Rs.25,000/- per month from 01.08.2016 till the handing over of the suit property by the defendant to plaintiff.
The decree be executed only after payment of appropriate court fee.
44. The plaintiff shall also be entitled to costs of the suit.
Decree sheet be prepared accordingly.
